All file operations are confined to the package's own source directory (after changing to the script's parent directory via `cd \`dirname $0\`/..`), and no network requests, external downloads, data exfiltration, or execution of attacker-controlled code occur.

This is standard upstream packaging/build infrastructure with no signs of injected malicious behavior. The use of `perl` for text replacement and the final invocation of another local build-script are entirely consistent with the project's stated purpose of managing library version numbers.

The PKGBUILD file defines a standard Arch Linux package build process for `lib32-sdl2-compat`, a compatibility layer allowing SDL2-based applications to use SDL3.
